## Summary

This pull request implements a solution for #2082: Check for all false positives, false negatives, warnings and errors in CI/CD and fix them all

- 116881 line(s) added

commits.messageBody:
Adding .gitkeep for PR creation (default mode).
This file will be removed when the task is complete.

Issue: https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/2082

… nothing

The Helm Release job has been green on every run since 2025-12-23 while
publishing nothing. The public chart repository is still at 0.38.8
(2025-12-11) though package.json is at 2.8.3 — ~7 months of no-op releases
reported as success.

Root cause: commit 5b7e60d7 converted helm-release.sh (which opened with
`set -euo pipefail`) to .mjs using command-stream's `$`, which resolves with
`.code` instead of throwing on a non-zero exit. The wrapping try/catch could
therefore never fire. In production `git checkout gh-pages` aborted because
gh-pages also carries the repo tree and the script had just rewritten
Chart.yaml; the failure was swallowed, the index was committed onto main,
`git push origin gh-pages` reported "Everything up-to-date", and the script
printed "released successfully!" and exited 0.

Verified experimentally (experiments/issue-2082-command-stream-throw.mjs):
command-stream's `$` returns code 1 without throwing.

- add scripts/run-command.lib.mjs with runStrict(), restoring `set -e`
  semantics on top of node:child_process (built-ins only, matching the
  hardening already applied in publish-to-npm.mjs for #2028)
- extract scripts/helm-release.lib.mjs so the flow is unit-testable
- publish from an isolated `git worktree` instead of switching branches in
  the dirty release checkout, removing the failure at its source
- copy the archive next to index.yaml so its download URL resolves
  (production emitted a .helm-packages/ URL that 404s)
- verify the pushed index really contains the released version, so a future
  regression is a red build rather than a silent no-op
- add HIVE_MIND_CI_VERBOSE=1 command tracing, off by default

tests/helm-release-2082.test.mjs pins all three properties. Confirmed by
mutation: restoring fail-soft semantics fails the test with
"a failing git command must abort the release".

Also compiles the full evidence pack and analysis into
dev/log/issues/2082/pulls/2083/.

Refs #2082
commits.messageHeadline: fix(ci): make Helm release fail loudly instead of silently publishing…

commits.messageBody:
… (#2082)

Finding F5 of issue #2082. Reproduced by tests/publish-verification-race-2082.test.mjs,
which fails against the previous implementation.

Root cause: retry granularity. `publishWithRetry` verified the version with a
single `npm view` immediately after publishing, and on a miss fell through to the
top of the retry loop — re-running the entire `npm run changeset:publish`. But the
npm registry serves metadata through a CDN, so a version can be invisible to
`npm view` for seconds after publish returns success (npm/cli#3424, #9043, #593).
A verification miss is therefore not evidence that the publish failed.

Observed in CI run 29647956700, a run that went GREEN:

    14:38:40  Publish attempt 1 of 3...
    14:38:46  success packages published successfully: @link-assistant/hive-mind@2.8.3
    14:38:46  Creating git tag... New tag: v2.8.3
    14:38:46  npm error code E404                       <- verified 0.3s after publish
    14:38:56  Publish attempt 2 of 3...                 <- re-ran the whole publish
    14:38:59  error npm error You cannot publish over the previously published versions: 2.8.3.
    14:39:09  Publish attempt 3 of 3...
    14:39:10  Verified @link-assistant/hive-mind@2.8.3 is live on npm

The release had already succeeded on attempt 1. It went green only because a
third attempt fit inside the budget, and only because by then there were no
changesets left for attempt 3 to publish. With one more second of CDN lag, or
one fewer retry, a completed release would have been reported as a failure.

Changes:
  - waitForVersionOnRegistry(): polls `npm view` with exponential backoff
    (2s -> 30s, ~90s total) instead of checking once.
  - A publish that reported success is never re-run. If verification ultimately
    fails the job fails — the #2028 false-positive protection is unchanged — but
    it fails on the verification, not by publishing again.
  - isVersionConflict(output, version): recognises npm's EPUBLISHCONFLICT for the
    version being released and treats it as "already landed", still subject to
    verification so a false claim cannot turn into a green release. Matched
    before the non-retryable classifier, since npm reports the conflict with a
    403 that would otherwise be misread as an auth failure.
  - Genuine publish failures are still retried exactly as before.
commits.messageHeadline: fix(ci): stop the npm publish/verify race republishing a live version…

commits.messageBody:
… (#2082)

Finding F4 of issue #2082 — the same fail-soft defect as F1, with a worse
consequence. Reproduced by tests/version-and-commit-2082.test.mjs, which fails
against the previous implementation.

Root cause: scripts/version-and-commit.mjs ran every git command as a bare
`await $\`...\``. command-stream's `$` resolves with `.code` instead of throwing,
so the try/catch wrapping main() could never fire.

`git push origin main` is racy by construction: the release workflow pushes the
version bump to main while merges and other runs push to the same branch. When
the push was rejected as non-fast-forward, the rejection was swallowed — the
script printed "Version bump committed and pushed to main", set
`version_committed=true`, and exited 0. The downstream publish job then worked
from a version that existed only in the runner's local checkout. Every command
before the push had the same problem: a failed `npm run changeset:version` or
`git commit` continued straight on to the push.

Changes:
  - scripts/version-and-commit.lib.mjs: the logic, extracted with injectable
    runner/output/logger so it can be unit-tested, with every command run
    through `runStrict` (restoring `set -e` semantics).
  - pushWithRebaseRetry(): a rejected push is rebased onto the new remote HEAD
    and retried (5 attempts, 3s apart) rather than assumed to have won the race.
    isNonFastForward() distinguishes a lost race from auth/network/protected-
    branch failures, which are not fixed by rebasing and so fail immediately
    with the real error.
  - `version_committed=true` is emitted only after a push that actually landed.
  - scripts/version-and-commit.mjs is now a thin argument-parsing CLI and no
    longer imports command-stream.

Verified by mutation: restoring the fail-soft runner makes the test fail with
"Missing expected rejection: a failing version bump must abort instead of
continuing to commit and push"; replacing the retry with a single push makes the
rejected-push case fail. Both are the production defects.
commits.messageHeadline: fix(ci): fail the release when the version bump is not pushed to main…

commits.messageBody:
… (#2082)

Finding F6 of issue #2082. 22 of the 26 jobs across the two workflows had no
`timeout-minutes`, so each inherited GitHub's 360-minute default: a job that
hangs on a prompt, a dead socket or a runaway test burns six hours of runner
time and then surfaces as a generic failure that looks nothing like a hang.
docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md already required an explicit timeout; nothing
enforced it.

Timeouts were chosen from measured job durations across the last four successful
release runs (29685608578, 29686630893, 29686761617, 29686947280) rather than
guessed. Observed maxima: test-suites 11m, Docker DinD amd64 7m, Docker amd64
6m, everything else under 2m. Applied limits give roughly 2-3x headroom
(test-suites 30, Docker merge jobs 30, release/instant-release 30, most checks
10-15). The four matrix Docker jobs already had 60 and are unchanged.

Enforcement lives in tests/ci-workflow-timeouts-2082.test.mjs, backed by
scripts/workflow-lint.lib.mjs. Nothing off the shelf does this: the zizmor
request (zizmorcore/zizmor#1023) and the actionlint request (rhysd/actionlint#49)
are both still open, so this is a custom check until one of them ships.

Two correctness details the check gets right, both of which would otherwise
trade one false result for another:
  - Jobs that call a reusable workflow via `uses:` are exempt. GitHub does not
    support `timeout-minutes` there; the timeout must live in the called
    workflow. Demanding one would be a false positive.
  - A `uses:` on a *step* is an action, not a reusable-workflow call, so it must
    not exempt the job. Confusing the two would silently exempt nearly every job
    in this repository.

The scanner is line-based rather than a YAML parse because js-yaml is only a
transitive dependency here and these checks must survive an unknown
node_modules state — the same constraint that shaped scripts/run-command.lib.mjs.
The result was cross-checked against a real YAML parse: 26 jobs, none missing.

The test also guards against passing vacuously, asserting both that workflow
files were found and that jobs were actually parsed.
commits.messageHeadline: fix(ci): require timeout-minutes on every job and enforce it in tests…

commits.messageBody:
…2082)

scripts/test-auto-fork-option.sh reported none of its three assertions:
each failed branch printed "Could not verify ..." and the script carried
on to exit 0.

This was not a latent risk. The marker the dry-run checks grep for first
appears ~32s into the run, because solve.mjs makes several GitHub API
calls before reaching the auto-fork decision — and the script killed the
command with `timeout 10s`. Both greps had been failing on every run
while the job stayed green. Reproduced locally: restoring the 10s
timeout now fails the script with exactly those two checks red.

- test-auto-fork-option.sh: realistic timeouts, every check asserts, and
  a hermetic --help check that does not depend on the network.
- check-file-line-limits.sh: a missing release.yml was a warning that
  skipped the check entirely; it is now an error.
- scripts/shell-lint.lib.mjs + tests: flag any `else` branch that reports
  a failure without failing. Branches that record the failure for a later
  check are exempt; deliberately non-fatal ones must say so with an
  explicit `# shell-lint: allow-nonfatal` marker and a reason.

ShellCheck does not cover this — an `else` that only echoes is valid
bash, so judging it needs repo-specific intent.
commits.messageHeadline: fix(ci): make shell test assertions fail the build, and enforce it (#…

commits.messageBody:
F14 — the concurrency policy was inverted:

    cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

It cancelled in-progress runs on main — the one branch that publishes —
and queued them everywhere else. A release cancelled between `npm
publish` and the `git push` of the version bump leaves the registry
ahead of the repository: the same split-brain state as F4 and F5,
reached by a different route. Now main queues and PR branches cancel,
which is also where the wasted runners were.

F13 — nine jobs guarded their `if:` with `always()`, which is true even
after a cancellation, so they defeated the policy above. release.yml
documents this rule at the top of the file (from the #1274 and #1278
case studies) but applied it only to the Docker jobs. Five used bare
`always()`; four paired it with a contradictory `!cancelled()`.

Verified semantics with a real YAML parse: exactly 9 of 25 jobs changed,
each only in the leading term, the other 16 byte-identical. Note that
`if: !cancelled() && ...` must be wrapped in ${{ }} — a leading `!` is a
YAML tag, and the previous always() spelling did not need this.

Also extracts two Docker blocks from release.yml into scripts/. The
timeout-minutes added in 0e4eb599 had pushed the file to 1512 lines,
over the 1500-line limit — which no CI run caught, because the missing
changeset failed the changeset gate and every other job was skipped.
That changeset is added here too.
commits.messageHeadline: fix(ci): stop cancelling releases mid-publish, drop always() (#2082)

commits.messageBody:
…(#2082)

The docker build and container-verification commands moved out of
release.yml into scripts/docker-pr-build.sh and
scripts/docker-pr-verify-containers.sh so the workflow stays under the
1500-line limit. Two contract tests asserted on the literal text inline in
release.yml and failed.

Rather than dropping the assertions, they now follow the indirection: the
job must invoke each script, AND each script must still contain the build
and verify commands. Asserting only the 'bash scripts/...' line would pass
against an empty script — verified by mutation: replacing
docker-pr-build.sh with a stub makes both tests fail.

Also adds the implementation log for issue #2082, recording the root cause,
fix and mutation check for F1/F3/F4/F5/F6/F13/F14, plus the gate-masking
effect that let a line-limit break reach main unnoticed.

Add development log for issue #2082 PR #2083

commits.messageBody:
npm run lint and eslint.config.mjs both scoped linting to src/, scripts/
and eslint-rules/. tests/ - the largest .mjs tree in the repo - was never
linted, so the lint job reported success while the test suite carried
real defects.

Enabling the glob surfaced them across 59 files: assert.match regexes
containing unescaped literal indentation, a catch that discarded the
original error, and a batch of unused bindings. These were not
hypothetical - they were live in tests CI runs on every push, and lint
stayed green. A false negative of the kind this issue is about.

Adds lint-covers-tests-2082.test.mjs pinning the coverage. It asserts
both npm run lint and the config files entry include each required
tree, since CI reads the former while --fix and editors read the
latter; drift means one of them lies about what is checked.

Change detection already gates lint on any .mjs change, so tests/ edits
trigger the job - no workflow change needed.
commits.messageHeadline: fix(ci): lint the tests/ tree and fix the defects it surfaced (#2082)

commits.messageBody:
…ell (#2082)

getClaudeEnv() builds the child environment by spreading process.env. For
adaptive-thinking-only models it explicitly deletes an inherited
MAX_THINKING_TOKENS, but nothing did the same for CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL.
The block below it only ever assigns, so on every path that computes no
level the parent's value survived into the child:

  - a model supporting no effort levels at all (haiku), which skips the
    enclosing supportsEffortLevel() branch entirely;
  - --think off on a non-adaptive model, where neither inner branch fires.

Claude Code exports this variable and hive-mind's agents run under Claude
Code, so the leak fired in the ordinary case: 'haiku --think high'
inherited effort=max for a model the codebase classifies as supporting
none. Fixed by mirroring the existing MAX_THINKING_TOKENS sanitisation.

This also made the suite return opposite verdicts for the same commit.
CI runs without the variable and stayed green; run the same tests inside
Claude Code and test-opus-47-model-support.mjs failed with 5 errors. It
now passes 166/0 under a polluted environment as well as a clean one.

Adds effort-level-env-leak-2082.test.mjs, which pins the leak, the
behaviour that had to survive the fix (issue #2032's lowest-effort
mapping for adaptive-only models on --think off), and the general
invariant that the result is independent of the ambient shell.

Three sibling variables leak identically and are confirmed present in the
agent environment (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT, CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW,
CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE). Deliberately left alone: no sanitisation
precedent, no failing test, and plausibly intentional user config. Recorded
in the dev log for an explicit decision rather than a silent change.

Also documents F21 (the tests/ lint gap), F22 (this leak) and F23 (a
pre-existing flake in test-issue-1209-overrides.mjs, root-caused to a
live unpkg.com fetch on every bot startup against a fixed 12s kill).
commits.messageHeadline: fix(config): stop CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL leaking from the parent sh…

commits.messageBody:
Commit fd3a44ef silenced timers/no-leaked-timers on this helper with
exitTimer.unref?.(). unref does not just make a timer cancellable - it
removes it from the handles keeping the event loop alive. That callback
is what settles the awaited closeScreenSession, so Node exited with the
await still pending: exit 13 on CI (run 29690457864, Node 24), and a
silent pass locally on Node 20, where unsettled top-level await is not
detected at all.

Capture the timer and clear it from inside its own callback instead. It
stays referenced until it fires, cb(0) settles the await, and the handle
is released - satisfying both the lint rule and the runtime.

Audited the other six files whose timers that lint pass touched: unref
was added in exactly one place, and every added clearTimeout runs after
the awaited work, so it can only no-op on an already-fired timer.

The suite was re-run under Node 24 rather than the sandbox's Node 20,
since the project's own engines field requires >=24 and the older
runtime cannot observe this failure mode.
commits.messageHeadline: fix(test): keep the fake spawn exit timer referenced (#2082)

commits.messageBody:
The changeset gate requires exactly one changeset added per PR, and run
29692835784 failed on it with two. That gate runs before everything else,
so test-suites and the rest of the checks were skipped rather than run -
the failure masked the state of every other job in the PR.

Folds the tests/ lint coverage and the CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL leak into
the existing CI/CD changeset. No content dropped.
commits.messageHeadline: chore(changeset): combine this PR's two changesets into one (#2082)

commits.messageBody:
F25: a PR can report green with its own code never executed by CI.
detect-code-changes.mjs diffs the latest push (before..after) on
synchronize, while branch protection reads the latest run - so a
docs-only commit pushed after a failed run leaves the heavy jobs
skipped and the PR green. Demonstrated on this PR: fd3a44ef ran
test-suites and failed, 1e04c45e carried the fix but was skipped
behind the changeset gate, and 15888c1e (changesets only) reported
success with the fix never executed. Not fixed here - every option
overturns behaviour issue #1665 introduced and pinned with a test,
which is a maintainer decision, so it is recorded with run IDs and
verbatim output instead.

R6: the previous claim - that the template lacks detectPublishFailure()
/ FAILURE_PATTERNS - was wrong, and is retracted. It came from reading
only publish-failure-classifier.mjs; the template defines both locally
in publish-to-npm.mjs. Filed the claim that does hold up instead:
template#105, the F5 publish/verify race, confirmed against the live
source and reported with a deterministic reproduction.

F23: a second instance, tests/test-hive-no-silent-failure.mjs, with a
5s budget against 7-9s CDN-bound startup. Confirmed pre-existing (3/3
failures on origin/main). CI's use-m warm-up step reduces but does not
remove it, which is the evidence that only local resolution fixes it.
commits.messageHeadline: docs(2082): record F25, correct the R6 upstream claim, extend F23

title: 'Check for all false positives, false negatives, warnings and errors in CI/CD and fix them all'
